summary: Backend regression suite passed all six tested workflows. Browser testing passed login, dashboard/demo visibility, mobile navigation, theme toggle, and logout, but project detail navigation is blocked by a React runtime crash.

minor.issue: No brute-force lockout or rate limiting is implemented after repeated failed logins.

ui_bugs.issue: Opening any project causes uncaught React runtime error `destroy is not a function`; project detail, manual records, analysis, upload review, and report UI become unusable.

integration_issues.issue: Clicking the seeded project row reaches the project route, then React crashes before [data-testid=add-record-button] renders.
Requested Google sign-in is not implemented; the login page explicitly says it can be connected when credentials are supplied.

issues: Recharts logs width/height -1 warnings during initial render; chart briefly renders without usable bars before layout settles.

action_items: Fix ProjectDetail useEffect cleanup: its callback currently returns the Axios Promise (`useEffect(load, [id])`), which React treats as a cleanup function and later invokes as destroy.
Retest project detail, manual strength/slump entry, analysis, upload review/import, and PDF download after the crash fix.
Implement Google sign-in or explicitly remove it from scope, and add brute-force protection for login.
Use an explicit CORS origin instead of backend/.env CORS_ORIGINS="*" with credentials.
critical_code_review_comments: `useEffect(load, [id])` is a critical async cleanup bug; wrap the request in an async effect and return only a real cleanup function.
The requested Google authentication integration is absent, not mocked.
CORS is configured with wildcard origin plus credentials, which is unsafe and incompatible with credentialed browser requests in standard CORS behavior.
seed_data_creation: Created TEST_CQAS_* project and TEST-prefixed strength/slump/import records during regression testing; these persisted because no delete endpoint or cleanup fixture exists.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth/session, seeded demo project, dashboard, API CRUD, deterministic analysis, Indonesian Excel mapping/import, PDF content type, invalid upload validation, mobile menu/theme, and logout were tested. Start by retesting project navigation after fixing the useEffect Promise cleanup crash.
rca of the issue: In frontend/src/App.js, ProjectDetail defines `const load = () => api.get(...).then(...)` and passes it directly to `useEffect(load, [id])`. React interprets the returned Axios Promise as the effect cleanup callback. On route/component lifecycle cleanup it invokes the Promise as a function, producing `TypeError: destroy is not a function` and preventing the detail screen from rendering.
